questions.question: What makes an internal knowledge assistant reliable?
options: A polished chat interface that makes the assistant feel responsive and trustworthy
Governed sources, a permission model, an evaluation sample, and a fallback path
An index that covers every document in SharePoint so nothing is ever missing
A context window large enough that whole documents fit without being chunked
questions.explanation: Internal assistants need source governance and answer evaluation. The lesson is explicit that source governance matters more than chatbot polish.

questions.question: A team wants a Confluence assistant. Where does this lesson locate the hard part?
options: Choosing an embedding model whose similarity scores match how colleagues phrase questions
Sizing the vector store so retrieval stays fast once the whole space has been indexed
Designing a chat interface that colleagues will prefer over searching Confluence directly
Knowing which sources are allowed, who owns them, what is stale, and how wrong answers get caught
questions.explanation: The lesson puts the difficulty in source governance rather than in the chat box: allowed sources, named owners, freshness, and a way to catch wrong answers.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A ranked source-readiness plan with matched controls and rationale
A production vector database populated from the team's document store
A permission model derived automatically from the source system's ACLs
A finished chatbot interface wired to the retrieval and fallback paths
questions.explanation: The artifact is a planning tool for source readiness - it ranks sources and matches controls before anything is indexed.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: An access boundary that keeps retrieval inside the permissions a user already has
A retrieval scope that ignores permissions so answers stay complete for every user
An evaluation set that is discarded once the assistant passes its first review
A source inventory with no named owner, so cleanup is a shared team responsibility
questions.explanation: Access boundaries keep retrieval aligned with permissions. Source owners, freshness rules, and answer evaluation are the other controls this lesson teaches.

questions.question: When should a knowledge assistant require a launch gate?
options: Only when the chat interface has to support more than one language at launch
Only when the source system is external rather than an internal wiki or drive
Only when the assistant is expected to answer more than a few hundred questions
When sensitive access, stale content, and missing evaluation create high risk
questions.explanation: High-risk source conditions - sensitive access, stale content, missing evaluation - require explicit launch review. Interface scope and query volume are not the risk signals here.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the intake template?
options: To record the assistant's answer quality after the first month of live use
To document the fallback path once uncertain answers start reaching support
To decide which sources are ready before any of them are indexed
To capture the user questions that the assistant was unable to answer correctly
questions.explanation: The intake template makes source readiness explicit before indexing, covering ownership, freshness, permissions, and evaluation.
